summary: For smooth proper rigid X over complete algebraically closed K/Q_p, Heuer constructs an exact tensor equivalence between pro-étale vector bundles and Tate-twisted Higgs bundles from a flat B_dR^+/ξ²-lift and an exponential agreeing with the series on its small domain. Naturality is for lifted morphisms and compatible exponentials; the derived cohomology comparison includes the lift-dependent Hodge–Tate splitting. The construction uses coherent-algebra Picard functors, a multiplicative Hodge–Tate sequence, representable reductions and rigidifications, locally p-divisible group exponentials, and canonical Higgs-field twisting. This fix separates early local/primitive comparison from later relative base change, generic perfectoid descent from rigid transfer, and the external algebraic/analytic/cohomological suppliers. It reuses the accepted H.0 Higgs and PD.7 all-torsion plans, pinned generic freeness/completion flatness, relative GAGA, analytic–étale descent, period sheaves, charts and shared Koszul algebra. Remaining source requests explicitly include the broader perfectoid basis, singular comparison/SNC supplier, full faithfulness over Spd K, general proper Picard representability, coherent comparison and exact finite pushforward. Source issues distinguish surviving published errors/gaps from three preprint slips corrected at publication; logarithmic normalization is a convention, not an additional error claim.

items.name: Scholze's pro-étale site with its completed structure sheaf
items.statement: For a rigid space X over a complete algebraically closed extension K of Q_p, use Scholze’s flattened site X_proét, the uncompleted sheaves O_X and O_X^+, their p-adic completions Ô_X^+ and Ô_X = Ô_X^+[1/p], and ν : X_proét → X_ét and λ : X_proét → X_an.
items.locator: §2.1, pp. 267–268; proof of Proposition 2.9, p. 273 (published version)
items.note: R4 reexports the site of AdicEtaleGeometry A1; P8:local-rational constructs rational period sheaves using the completed integral sheaf of AI.3. The broader perfectoid-basis assertion is a separate missing item 49, with an explicit requested extension of AI.3 beyond its smooth formal generic-fibre scope. Neither the basis nor that widening is counted as already planned here.

items.name: Pro-étale vector bundles on a rigid space
items.statement: For rigid X/K with completed structure sheaf Ô_X, a pro-étale vector bundle is a finite locally free Ô_X-module on Scholze’s flattened X_proét.
items.locator: Definition 1.2(1), p. 262; §2.1, p. 268 (published version)
items.note: The perfectoid site-equivalence theorem and its transfer to rigid X are items 50 and 51; this definition belongs downstream of the site, completed sheaf and basis, in the Simpson Part II.

items.name: Higgs bundles on a smooth rigid space
items.statement: With Ω̃_X := Ω^1_X(−1) and Ω̃^k = ∧^kΩ̃, a Higgs bundle is (E, θ) with E an analytic vector bundle and θ : E → E ⊗ Ω̃_X O_X-linear with θ ∧ θ = 0; equivalently an O_X-algebra map T_X := Sym^•Ω̃^∨ → End(E).
items.locator: Definition 1.2(2), p. 262; Definition 2.1, p. 267; Definition 4.1, p. 297 (published version)
items.note: The accepted HodgeStructuresPartII design now has H.0/twisted-higgs on general ringed differential sites, including T=O_X(−1). Reuse it; the old Part II proposal is now a source route to H.0, not another design.

items.name: Exponentials for K
items.statement: Put α = 1/(p−1) for p ≥ 3 and α = 2 for p = 2. The convergent exponential is a group isomorphism exp : p^α m_K → 1+p^α m_K; log : 1+m_K → K is surjective. An exponential for K is a group homomorphism Exp : K → 1+m_K satisfying log∘Exp = id and Exp|_{p^α m_K} = exp. This agreement implies continuity.
items.locator: §3.3, Definition 3.19, p. 293 (published version)
items.note: Existence is the separately extracted Heuer–Werner–Zhang Lemma 6.2, item 83; continuity by itself does not imply agreement with the series (E18). Fractional p-powers mean valuation bounds, or a chosen element of that valuation in algebraically closed K.

items.name: B_dR^+/ξ²-lifts and their existence for proper spaces
items.statement: For smooth X/K, a B_dR^+(K)/ξ²-lift is a flat adic thickening 𝕏 over Spa(B_dR^+(K)/ξ²) together with its identification of the K-fibre with X. A smooth proper X admits such a lift by Guo, Hodge–Tate decomposition for non-smooth spaces, Proposition 7.4.4. If X descends to a smooth model over a complete discretely valued L ⊆ K with perfect residue field, base change along the canonical L → B_dR^+(K)/ξ² gives the model-induced lift.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, p. 261; §1.3, pp. 264–265; Definition 2.12, p. 275 (published version)
items.note: Point lifts and the formal smoothness used in the construction are a separate input, item 74. They are points of 𝕏, not points of X over the period thickening.

items.name: Local Hodge–Tate comparison and smooth proper primitive comparison
items.statement: Let K be complete algebraically closed over Q_p and X/K smooth rigid. With Ω̃_X^n = Ω_X^n(−n), R^nν_*Ô_X ≅ Ω̃_X^n, compatibly with cup products and exterior powers. Normalize degree one by the Kummer boundary O_X^× → R^1ν_*Ẑ_p(1): under R^1ν_*Ô_X(1) ≅ Ω_X^1 it is dlog. Thus the coordinate Kummer class on a toric chart maps to dT_i/T_i (Scholze survey, Proposition 3.23 and Lemma 3.24, PDF pp. 21–22). For smooth proper X, primitive comparison gives RΓ(X_proét,Ô_X) ≅ RΓ_ét(X,Q_p)⊗_{Q_p}K (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 5.1).
items.locator: §1.2, (1), p. 263; proofs of Proposition 2.9(ii), p. 274, and Corollary 2.19, p. 279 (published version)
items.note: The proper singular/non-reduced F_p finiteness and almost comparison needed for X′ are split into item 71, with the rigid resolution supplier in item 72. Route 1 requests an EARLY P8:local-rational extension, as in BMS18 route 14; these are inputs to CP.3, not outputs of the later P8 proper-comparison suffix. CP.3 supplies a spectral sequence, whereas the lift-dependent splitting is item 43 with V=Ô_X.

items.name: The Faltings extension
items.statement: Let X=X_0⊗_L K, where X_0 is smooth rigid over a complete discretely valued extension L/Q_p with perfect residue field. On X_proét, the arithmetic Faltings extension 0 → Ô_X → E → ν^*Ω̃_X^1 → 0 is the (−1)-twist of 0 → Ô_X(1) → gr^1 OB_dR^+ → Ô_X⊗_{O_X}Ω_X^1 → 0 (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Corollary 6.14).
items.locator: Remark 2.17, p. 278 (published version)
items.note: The exact supplier is P8:local-rational/faltings-extension. Without the arithmetic model the analogue depends on a lift 𝕏 and is constructed from the dual Higgs–Tate torsor in item 21 (Remark 2.17).

items.name: The rigid analytic Picard functor
items.statement: For proper rigid X/K, Pic_X is the étale sheafification on Rig^sm_K of S ↦ H^1_an(X×S,O^×); equivalently use étale line bundles. Its general rigid representability is conjectural. If X=X_0^an for a proper K-scheme X_0, its Picard functor identifies with Pic_{X_0/K}^an.
items.locator: §2.2, p. 268 (published version)
items.note: The comparison of analytic and étale line bundles is planned in item 60. Proper-scheme Picard representability is the missing general input 55, not the abelian degree-zero A2 theorem; relative coherent GAGA is planned in item 56. These give the algebraisable example in Theorem 2.4 and are not assumptions of the always-representable reduction in item 26.

items.name: Kiehl's proper mapping theorem
items.statement: For proper X, coherent cohomology H^i(X, B) is finite-dimensional over K.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 3.5, p. 287; §2.3, p. 274 (published version)

items.name: Coherent base change for a constant proper family
items.statement: Let X/K be smooth proper, B a coherent O_X-module, and Y/K smooth rigid. Pull B to X×Y. Coherent base change and the splitting Ω̃_{X×Y}=pr_X^*Ω̃_X⊕pr_Y^*Ω̃_Y identify H^0(X×Y,Ω̃_{X×Y}⊗pr_X^*B) with (H^0(X,Ω̃_X⊗B)⊗_K O(Y)) ⊕ (B(X)⊗_K H^0(Y,Ω̃_Y)).
items.locator: Heuer §2.3, pp. 274–275; Heuer, The relative Hodge–Tate spectral sequence for rigid analytic spaces, Corollary 3.10 and Theorem 3.18(b).
items.note: Item 44 retains the pro-étale completed-sheaf base-change statement at the later P8 suffix. The pro-étale site is downstream of R3 in the assembled graph; finding RT-PAPER-HEUER-25/24 was rejected and is not applied.

items.name: Lemma 2.7: integral models of coherent algebras
items.statement: Let X/K be quasi-compact smooth rigid and B a coherent O_X-module on X_an. There exists a finitely presented O_X^+-module B_0 with B_0[1/p]≅B; for a coherent algebra B, choose B_0 as an O_X^+-algebra using a finite formal model of Spa_{O_X}(B)→X. Pull B_0 to X_ét and put B^+=B_0/B_0[p^∞], its image in B. Since B_0 may have unbounded p-power torsion, B^+ need not be coherent. The formal module and finite-algebra suppliers are items 62–63 (Abbes Proposition 4.8.18(ii), Proposition 5.9.17 and Theorem 2.11.5, as restated publicly by Heuer).
items.locator: Lemma 2.7, p. 270 (published version)
items.note: B is analytic/étale; ℬ=ν^*B is its completed pro-étale pullback. The pro-étale integral sheaves are defined in item 18, rather than conflated with B_0 and B^+. The module- and finite-morphism formal-model inputs cited from Abbes are extracted separately in items 62–63; only their public restatement in Heuer Lemma 2.7 was read, not the uncleared Abbes book.

items.name: Proposition 2.18: proper base change for the étale cohomology of a proper rigid space
items.statement: Let K be complete algebraically closed over Q_p, n ≥ 1 and m ≥ 0. If g:Z→Spa(K) is a proper rigid space, without smoothness or reducedness assumptions, then R^m g_{ét*}(Z/nZ), viewed on Rig^sm_{K,ét}, is the constant sheaf with value H^m_ét(Z,Z/nZ).
items.locator: Proposition 2.18, p. 279 (published version)
items.note: Heuer Proposition 2.18 is the constant-family specialization of Bhatt–Hansen Theorem 3.15, not its full Cartesian statement. Items 85–87 extract that statement and its p-primary suppliers. H3’s prime-to-p theorem alone does not provide n=p^a; the mod-p Part II also needs constructibility/overconvergence, the rank-one stalk formula and proper extension invariance. Z=X′ may be singular or non-reduced. The accepted ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomologyPartII packet now states this exact target at PD.7/heuer-constant-cohomology-sheaf; reuse it, retaining its explicit G3 singular-comparison proof-supplier gap.

items.name: Exactness of finite pushforward
items.statement: For a finite morphism f:Y′→Y of rigid spaces and a geometric point ξ of Y with algebraically closed field, (f_{ét*}F)_ξ ≅ ∏_{ξ_i over ξ} F_{ξ_i}, with a finite fibre. Hence f_{ét*} is exact and commutes with arbitrary base change; in particular H^n_ét(Y,f_*O_{Y′}^×) ≅ H^n_ét(Y′,O_{Y′}^×).
items.locator: Heuer Lemma 2.20, p. 280; Huber, Étale Cohomology of Rigid Analytic Varieties and Adic Spaces, Proposition 2.6.3, pp. 139–140 (cleared copy).
items.note: Requested source extension of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0. Its stalk-formula-strict-localisation node does not itself state the finite-fibre acyclicity lemma; a quotation in another node is not a planned target. This extraction does not change the H0 packet.

items.name: Banach open mapping theorem
items.statement: A surjective continuous linear map of Banach spaces over K is open.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.8(3), p. 272 (published version)
items.note: Read ContinuousLinearMap.isOpenMap in Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Banach.lean at 082e2d3, including the complete normed-space hypotheses. No new Lean file or instantiation was compiled.

items.name: Analytic p-divisible groups and the corrected identity-component criterion
items.statement: A commutative rigid group G/K is analytic p-divisible if G=Ĝ and [p]:G→G is finite surjective. It is locally p-divisible if it contains an open analytic p-divisible subgroup. If [p]:G→G is surjective as a morphism of étale sheaves, then Ĝ^0 is analytic p-divisible. Equivalently, local p-divisibility is surjectivity of log_G:Ĝ→Lie(G)⊗G_a. If π_0(G) is finite, surjectivity of [p] also implies that [p] on G is finite étale.
items.locator: Heuer §3.3, p. 293; Heuer–Werner–Zhang, p-adic Simpson correspondences for principal bundles in abelian settings, arXiv:2308.13456v2, Definition 6.8 and Proposition 6.10, pp. 33–35.
items.note: The whole Ĝ need not be analytic p-divisible with infinitely many components (E15). Separate inputs are Fargues’s Lie description and étale/finite criteria (77–78, 81), representability of topological p-torsion (79), and the logarithm sequence (80).

items.name: Theorem 3.20 (Heuer–Werner–Zhang): exponentials of rigid groups
items.statement: Let K be complete algebraically closed over Q_p and G a commutative LOCALLY p-divisible rigid group over K. An exponential Exp for K in the sense of item 4 induces a continuous homomorphism Exp_G:Lie(G)→Ĝ(K) splitting log_G on K-points, naturally in G.
items.locator: Heuer–Werner–Zhang, p-adic Simpson correspondences for principal bundles in abelian settings, arXiv:2308.13456v2, Theorem 6.12, p. 35; used as Heuer Theorem 3.20, p. 293.
items.note: This is the version proved by the cited theorem. Heuer’s weaker K-point-surjectivity hypothesis is a citation/hypothesis gap, not a refuted K-point conclusion (E16). The connected groups P_𝕏^0 and (P_𝕏^M)^0 used in Theorems 3.2/3.22 satisfy the stronger sheaf-surjectivity criterion, so the construction uses this proven version.

items.name: Definition 2.2: the pro-étale Picard functor of a coherent algebra
items.statement: For proper rigid X/K and a commutative coherent O_X-algebra B, set ℬ=ν^*B and X′=Spa_{O_X}(B), finite over X. On X×S pull back B and use the completed pro-étale sheaf ℬ. Pic_{ℬ,proét} is the étale sheafification on Rig^sm_K of S ↦ H^1_proét(X×S,ℬ^×)/H^1_proét(S,π_{S,proét*}ℬ^×).
items.locator: Definition 2.2, pp. 268–269; §1.4, p. 265 (published version)

items.name: Lemma 2.8: comparison modulo p^k and the exponential
items.statement: Let X/K be smooth quasi-compact, B coherent and B_0 a finitely presented O_X^+-model as in item 11. Write B^+=B_0/B_0[p^∞]⊆B on X_ét; on X_proét put ℬ_0=λ^*B_0=ν^{-1}B_0⊗_{ν^{-1}O_X^+}Ô_X^+ and ℬ^+=ℬ_0/ℬ_0[p^∞]⊆ℬ=ν^*B. For every integer k, ℬ/p^kℬ^+ ≅ ν^{-1}(B/p^kB^+), and its derived ν-pushforward is B/p^kB^+. For commutative algebras, ℬ^×/(1+2pℬ^+) ≅ ν^{-1}(B^×/(1+2pB^+)); the same pullback argument works with 1+pℬ^+. The exponential gives pℬ^+≅1+pℬ^+ for p>2, and 4ℬ^+≅1+4ℬ^+ for p=2.
items.locator: Lemma 2.8, pp. 271–272 (published version)
items.note: Using 2p uniformly supplies the quotient needed for the logarithmic normalization in items 19–20, including p=2. Pullback of étale quotient sheaves uses item 48; this is not an assertion that B^+ is coherent.

items.name: Proposition 2.9: pushforward of ν*B and of its units
items.statement: For smooth quasi-compact rigid X/K and coherent O_X-module B, the completed pullback satisfies ℬ=ν^*B≅Lν^*B and R^nν_*ℬ≅B⊗_{O_X}Ω̃_X^n. For a commutative coherent algebra B, ν_*ℬ^×=B^×; for n≥1, R^nν_*ℬ^×≅R^nν_*ℬ≅B⊗Ω̃_X^n, where the first identification is induced by log on 1+2pℬ^+≅2pℬ^+⊆ℬ.
items.locator: Proposition 2.9, pp. 272–274 (published version)
items.note: The unscaled logarithm fixes the normalization. Inverting exp(p·−) and then including ℬ^+ would divide this identification by p (by 4 for the p=2 choice). The source asserts an isomorphism without fixing that convention; this is not recorded as a false theorem or a literal misprint.

items.name: Corollary 2.11: additive and multiplicative Hodge–Tate sequences
items.statement: For smooth quasi-compact rigid X/K and coherent B, Leray gives the functorial left-exact sequence 0→H^1_ét(X,B)→H^1_proét(X,ℬ)→H^0(X,Ω̃_X⊗B), with last arrow HT_B. For a commutative coherent algebra B there is likewise 0→H^1_ét(X,B^×)→H^1_proét(X,ℬ^×)→H^0(X,Ω̃_X⊗B), with last arrow HTlog. Normalize HTlog by log, so HTlog∘exp=HT_B on classes from H^1_proét(X,2pℬ^+).
items.locator: Corollary 2.11, p. 274 (published version)
items.note: No surjectivity is claimed at this stage; Theorem 2.4 supplies it later for smooth proper X. See E9 and the convention recorded in item 19.

items.name: Definitions 2.12–2.14 and Lemmas 2.13, 2.16: the Higgs–Tate torsor
items.statement: Let X/K be any smooth rigid space and 𝕏 a flat B_dR^+/ξ²-lift. The sheaf L_𝕏 of B_dR^+/ξ²-algebra homomorphisms λ^{-1}O_𝕏→B_dR^+/ξ² lifting λ^{-1}O_X→Ô_X is a torsor under ν^*Ω̃_X^∨, naturally in the lifted pair. For coherent B and θ:Ω̃_X^∨→B, pushout gives an additive ℬ-torsor L_{𝕏,B,θ}. On a toric chart its cocycle is γ↦Σ_i c_i(γ)∂_i, with ∂_i dual to dT_i/T_i. If X=X_0⊗_L K with L complete discretely valued of perfect residue field and 𝕏 the model-induced lift, its class is dual to the twisted arithmetic Faltings extension of item 7 (Remark 2.17).
items.locator: §2.4, Definition 2.12–Lemma 2.16, pp. 275–278 (published version); Remark 2.17
items.note: The period sheaf’s square-zero kernel is item 52 and formal smooth lifting is item 74. No quasi-compactness is imposed on Definition 2.12. In the coordinates used to prove Lemma 2.16 the lift adds T_i a_i, not a_i, for a logarithmic dual-basis coefficient a_i (E19).

items.name: Proposition 2.15: the lift splits the Hodge–Tate sequence
items.statement: For smooth rigid X/K, a flat lift 𝕏 and coherent B in the quasi-compact setting of the Hodge–Tate sequence, θ↦[L_{𝕏,B,θ}] defines a natural section s_{𝕏,B}:H^0(X,B⊗Ω̃_X)→H^1_proét(X,ℬ) of HT_B, functorial in B and lifted pairs (X,𝕏).
items.locator: Proposition 2.15, p. 277 (published version)
items.note: The proof uses the Kummer/dlog characterization of the degree-one Hodge–Tate isomorphism in item 6 (Scholze survey Lemma 3.24), not merely an unspecified isomorphism R^1ν_*Ô≅Ω̃.

items.name: Theorem 2.4 (Theorem 1.5): the multiplicative Hodge–Tate sequence of B
items.statement: For smooth proper rigid X/K and commutative coherent O_X-algebra B with ℬ=ν^*B and X′=Spa_{O_X}(B), put A_B=H^0(X,B⊗Ω̃_X)⊗_K G_a. There is a natural short exact sequence 0→Pic_{X′}→Pic_{ℬ,proét}→^{HTlog}A_B→0 on Rig^sm_{K,ét}, split over an open subgroup. If Pic_{X′} is representable, this is a sequence of rigid groups; its Lie sequence is 0→H^1_an(X,B)→H^1_proét(X,ℬ)→H^0(X,B⊗Ω̃_X)→0, and [p] on Pic_{ℬ,proét}^0 is finite étale. On K-points, 0→Pic(X′)→H^1_proét(X,ℬ^×)→H^0(X,B⊗Ω̃_X)→0.
items.locator: Theorem 2.4, p. 269; proofs pp. 274–282; Remark 2.22, p. 281 (published version)
items.note: Representability transfers by the argument of Heuer, Diamantine Picard functors, Corollary 2.9 (item 61); Lie comparison uses the separately stated coherent analytic–étale input 65. The algebraisable example uses 55–56. The last term is a tensor product, as in the published Remark 2.22; the preprint cross is E17.

items.name: Corollary 2.19 and Lemma 2.21: the boundary map vanishes
items.statement: Let P=Pic_{X′} be representable, with X′ proper as above, and G=P^0. Then [p]:G→G is finite étale, a torsor under G[p]=G∩H^1_ét(X′,μ_p). On all P the kernel is H^1_ét(X′,μ_p); its image is an open and closed subgroup containing G. If Q is an étale sheaf quotient of a locally constant sheaf, every morphism from a connected rigid space to Q is constant (Lemma 2.21). This makes the boundary ∂:A_B→R^2π′_{ét*}O^× vanish.
items.locator: Corollary 2.19, p. 279; Lemma 2.21, pp. 280–281 (published version)
items.note: Corollary 2.19 overstates the identity-component torsor group (E14). Repair surjectivity sheaf-theoretically: with N=P/G and Q=coker([p]:G→G), constant proper-base-change Kummer boundary vanishes on G. Snake gives N[p]↠Q, so Lemma 2.21 makes the surjection G→Q constant and zero. Thus Q=0. Fargues’s Lie criterion and finite-kernel criterion yield finite étaleness. The open/closed image on P is the kernel of a locally constant Kummer boundary, not an arbitrary open analytic subgroup.

items.name: Lemma 2.23: the Lie algebra of the Picard variety
items.statement: Let X/K be smooth proper and B a commutative coherent O_X-algebra, with finite X′=Spa_{O_X}(B). If Pic_{X′} on Rig^sm_{K,ét} is representable, then Lie(Pic_{X′})≅H^1_an(X′,O_{X′})≅H^1_an(X,B). This uses the Lie/Hom description (77), Gerritzen’s disc Picard input (57), and the coherent analytic–étale comparison (65), not testing the functor on non-smooth dual-number objects outside its domain.
items.locator: Lemma 2.23, p. 282 (published version)

items.name: Theorem 3.2: a representable reduction of structure group
items.statement: Let X/K be smooth proper, B a commutative coherent O_X-algebra, ℬ=ν^*B, and 𝕏 a flat B_dR^+/ξ²-lift. Push out L_{𝕏,B} by exp:ℬ→ℬ^×[1/p] to obtain a splitting e_𝕏:A_B→Pic_{ℬ,proét}[1/p] of HTlog[1/p]. The equalizer P_𝕏=eq(can,e_𝕏∘HTlog) is a rigid group and sits in 0→Pic_{X′}[p^∞]→P_𝕏→A_B→0. Its Lie algebra is A_B(K); [p] on P_𝕏^0 and HTlog:P_𝕏^0→A_B are surjective.
items.locator: Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, pp. 282–285 (published version)
items.note: No O_X-torsion-free hypothesis on B is needed in Theorem 3.2; that extra condition begins in §3.2. The equalizer uses exp after inverting p and does not assume Pic_{X′} itself is representable. This supplies the stronger local-p-divisibility hypothesis used by item 16.

items.name: Lemmas 3.3–3.4: units of finite K-algebras
items.statement: For a finite commutative K-algebra A with connected spectrum and nilradical η(A), (A ⊗ R)^× ≅ (η(A) ⊗ R) × R^× functorially; for A ↪ A′ finite, (A ⊗ O)^× is represented by G_a^r × G_m^s and (A ⊗ O)^× → (A′ ⊗ O)^× is split injective with cokernel of the same form, also on S_proét.
items.locator: Lemmas 3.3–3.4, pp. 286–287 (published version)

items.name: Lemma 3.5 and Definition 3.6: rigidifying sets of points
items.statement: For a torsion-free coherent O_X-module B on smooth proper X/K there is a finite B-rigidifying set M⊆X(K), meaning H^0(X,B)→∏_{x∈M}B|_x is injective. A finite multiset is rigidifying by the same test. A finite set 𝕄⊆𝕏(B_dR^+/ξ²) is rigidifying when its reduction multiset M in X(K) is. Torsion-freeness is necessary; one point need not suffice.
items.locator: Lemma 3.5 and Definition 3.6, p. 287 (published version)
items.note: For the generic-freeness step choose a connected affinoid component where the nonzero section remains nonzero: smoothness makes its ring a normal domain. Apply item 64 there and then torsion-freeness. An arbitrary disconnected smooth affinoid need not be a domain (E20). A lifted point belongs to 𝕏; different lifts of one K-point give a multiset after reduction.

items.name: Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.8
items.statement: For B an O_X-torsion-free coherent O_X-algebra on the smooth proper rigid space X and S ∈ Rig^sm_K: Pic_{B,proét}(S) = H^1_proét(X × S, ℬ^×)/H^1_proét(S, π_*ℬ^×) = H^0(S, R^1π_{S*}ℬ^×) without sheafification (Proposition 3.7); for a B-rigidifying multiset M the specialisation H^0(X × S, ℬ) → ∏_{x∈M} B|_x ⊗ O(S) is injective, and Q_M = (∏_{x∈M} B|_x ⊗ O)^×/H^0(X × S, ℬ^×) is a sheaf represented by G_a^r × G_m^s (Lemma 3.8).
items.locator: Proposition 3.7 and Lemma 3.8, p. 288 (published version)

items.name: Rigidified invertible B-modules and their Picard functors
items.statement: Let X/K be smooth proper, B a commutative coherent O_X-torsion-free algebra, ℬ=ν^*B, and M a finite B-rigidifying multiset of K-points. Over S∈Rig^sm_K, an M-rigidified invertible ℬ-module is (L,(α_x:L|_{x×S}≅ℬ|_{x×S})_{x∈M}); an isomorphism respects every α_x. Between two such objects there is at most one isomorphism. Their isomorphism classes form a presheaf of abelian groups by tensor product, denoted Pic^M_{ℬ,proét}; it is an étale sheaf. P_𝕏^M is its fibre product with P_𝕏 over Pic_{ℬ,proét}, not the whole rigidified Picard functor.
items.locator: Definition 3.9–Lemma 3.13, pp. 288–289 (published version)
items.note: Uniqueness uses the injective specialization in Lemma 3.8. For M empty and B=O_X, multiplication by a nontrivial K-unit gives a counterexample to unqualified uniqueness. Definitions 3.9/3.12 and Lemmas 3.11/3.13 supply the distinct contracts.

items.name: Theorem 3.14: rigidified Picard functors
items.statement: Let X/K be smooth proper, B a commutative coherent torsion-free O_X-algebra, M B-rigidifying, and 𝕏 a flat lift. There is an exact sequence 0→Q_M→Pic^M_{ℬ,proét}→Pic_{ℬ,proét}→0 on Rig^sm_{K,ét}; if the last term is representable, so is Pic^M. The pulled-back sequence 0→Q_M→P_𝕏^M→P_𝕏→0 is exact already on Rig^sm_{K,an}, so P_𝕏^M is always a rigid group.
items.locator: Theorem 3.14, pp. 289–291 (published version)
items.note: The analytic-local triviality of the Q_M≅G_a^r×G_m^s torsors uses the planned analytic–étale comparisons in item 60, not an unextracted p-adic Simpson input.

items.name: Additive rigidified functors and the canonical Lie algebra section
items.statement: Let X/K be smooth proper with lift 𝕏, B a commutative coherent torsion-free O_X-algebra, and M a finite B-rigidifying multiset. The additive rigidification functor LP_𝕏^M classifies a:S→A_B with rigidifications of the additive ℬ-torsor a^*L_{𝕏,B}, modulo its global translations. There is an exact sequence of rigid vector groups 0→LQ_M→LP_𝕏^M→A_B→0 and a natural identification Lie(P_𝕏^M)=LP_𝕏^M(K). If M′⊇M, the derivative of the forgetful map P_𝕏^{M′}→P_𝕏^M is the corresponding forgetful map on LP evaluated on K (Lemma 3.17(2)). A finite lifted set 𝕄⊆𝕏(B_dR^+/ξ²) with reduction multiset M gives the section s_{𝕏,𝕄}:A_B(K)→Lie(P_𝕏^M) by the induced trivializations at each lifted point.
items.locator: Definition 3.15–Definition 3.18, pp. 291–292 (published version)
items.note: This derivative comparison supplies independence of the finite lifted rigidification set in Theorem 3.22. Existence of the individual lifts is item 74; their choice is additional data. The proof’s reference for the rigidified P^M is corrected in E21.

items.name: Theorem 3.22: exponential invertible B-modules
items.statement: Let X/K be smooth proper, 𝕏 a flat B_dR^+/ξ²-lift and Exp an exponential as in item 4. Every O_X-coherent torsion-free T_X=Sym_{O_X}(Ω̃_X^∨)-algebra B has a canonically rigidified invertible ℬ=ν^*B-module L_B with HTlog(L_B)=τ_B and class Exp(τ_B)∈P_𝕏(K). For a morphism B→B′ of such T_X-algebras, L_B⊗_ℬℬ′≅L_{B′}, compatibly with composition. For continuous K→K′, a compatible exponential Exp′, smooth proper X′/K′ with lift 𝕏′, and a morphism f:X′→X with lift f̃:𝕏′→𝕏, let B′ be the maximal O_{X′}-torsion-free quotient of f^*B; then f^*L_B⊗_{f^*ℬ}ℬ′≅L_{B′}, compatibly with composition and algebra maps. Given B→B_1,B→B_2, let B_3 be the maximal torsion-free quotient of B_1⊗_B B_2, endowed with the T_X-action whose tautological section is τ_{B_1}⊗1+1⊗τ_{B_2}. Then (L_{B_1}⊗_{ℬ_1}ℬ_3)⊗_{ℬ_3}(ℬ_3⊗_{ℬ_2}L_{B_2})≅L_{B_3}, compatibly with triple products and pullback.
items.locator: Definition 3.21 and Theorem 3.22, pp. 294–297; Remark 3.23 (published version)
items.note: The canonical rigidifications and their compatibility give uniqueness; an unrigidified invertible module can have automorphisms. Tensor compatibility uses the specified sum action, not an unspecified product. See Theorem 3.22(1–4), pp. 294–297.

items.name: Definition 4.1: the spectral algebra of a Higgs field
items.statement: For a Higgs bundle (E,θ) on smooth rigid X/K, the image B_θ of T_X→End(E) is a commutative coherent O_X-algebra and is O_X-torsion-free as a submodule of End(E). The tautological τ_θ∈H^0(X,B_θ⊗Ω̃_X) maps to θ. In the smooth proper lifted setting, if T_X→B′→B_θ with B′ coherent AND O_X-torsion-free, Theorem 3.22(2) identifies ν^*E⊗_{ℬ_θ}L_{B_θ} with ν^*E⊗_{ℬ′}L_{B′}.
items.locator: Definition 4.1 and Remark 4.2, pp. 297–298 (published version)
items.note: Remark 4.2 needs the torsion-free condition for its invocation of the canonical L_{B′} construction (E24). Its B_τ subscript in v3 is corrected to B_θ in the journal (E23).

items.name: Chart coordinates, integral Higgs lattice and quantitative smallness
items.statement: Fix a toric chart f:U→T^d on a smooth affinoid U/K, with Δ=Z_p(1)^d-tower Ũ→U. The logarithmic dual coordinate basis identifies ρ_f:H^0(U,Ω̃_U)≅Hom_cts(Δ,O(U)), and tensoring gives ρ_{f,B} for coherent B. The inverse image of Hom_cts(Δ,O_U^+) gives the chart-dependent integral lattice Ω̃_U^+. Smallness for the fixed-chart local correspondence means the quantitative integral bound of Heuer, Moduli spaces, arXiv:2207.13819v2, Definition 6.2 (with the constant of Proposition 5.5), for both pro-étale and Higgs bundles. Every such bundle becomes small after a suitable étale localization and sufficiently far passage up the toric tower.
items.locator: Definition 4.3, pp. 298–299 (published version)
items.note: Existence of the toric chart is planned separately in item 70; the generic perfectoid tower/basis is item 49. The lattice and fixed-chart bound depend on f. Lemma 6.4 keeps the required constant controlled while passing up the tower. Exponential convergence in 2p alone need not attain that bound; E22 records the qualification.

items.name: Theorem 4.4: the local correspondence (Faltings; Heuer)
items.statement: For smooth toric affinoid U/K with a fixed chart f, LS_f is an exact equivalence from pro-étale vector bundles small with respect to f to Higgs bundles small with respect to f. Its INVERSE sends (E,θ) to V with V(Ũ)=O(Ũ)⊗_{O(U)}E(U) and γ·(a⊗x)=γ(a)⊗exp(ρ_{f,End(E)}(θ)(γ))x. For any pro-étale vector bundle V, ν_*End(V) is coherent (Corollary 4.5).
items.locator: Heuer Theorem 4.4 and Corollary 4.5, pp. 299–300; Faltings, A p-adic Simpson correspondence, §3; Heuer, Moduli spaces, arXiv:2207.13819v2, Theorem 6.5(2), pp. 34–35.
items.note: The formula describes LS_f^{-1}, correcting E10. The displayed tensor product is over O(U); LS_f^{-1} is only defined on its f-small domain. Coherence of End is local for the étale topology and follows after making V small.

items.name: Lemma 4.6 and Proposition 4.7: the local correspondence as twisting
items.statement: Let X/K be smooth rigid, B a coherent commutative O_X-algebra, ℬ=ν^*B and L invertible over ℬ with τ=HTlog(L). Étale locally on toric charts f:U→T^d, arrange ρ_{f,B}(τ)(Δ)⊆2pB^+(U). Then L is locally isomorphic to L_{τ,f}, descended from O(Ũ)⊗_{O(U)}B(U) with action γ·(a⊗x)=γ(a)⊗exp(ρ_{f,B}(τ)(γ))x. For a Higgs bundle (E,θ) SMALL WITH RESPECT TO f and B=B_θ, there is étale locally an isomorphism LS_f^{-1}(E,θ)≅ν^*E⊗_ℬL_{τ_θ,f} (Proposition 4.7).
items.locator: Lemma 4.6 and Proposition 4.7, pp. 299–300 (published version)
items.note: The 2p bound in Lemma 4.6 ensures convergence; when the local correspondence is invoked, go further up the tower until the actual Definition 6.2 bound is met (Heuer Moduli spaces v2, Lemma 6.4). In comparing two charts in Theorem 4.8, arrange the required smallness for both. Do not infer it solely from convergence. The action includes the factor x (E11).

items.name: Theorem 4.8 and Corollaries 4.10–4.11: the canonical Higgs field (Rodríguez Camargo)
items.statement: For smooth rigid X/K every pro-étale vector bundle V has a canonical Higgs field θ_V on X_proét, functorial in V and X; on a toric chart where V is f-small it is the field obtained from LS_f(V). It vanishes exactly when V is étale-locally trivial as an analytic vector bundle. If V=ν^*E⊗_ℬL with B=B_θ and HTlog(L)=τ_B, this field is ν^*θ_E⊗_ℬL.
items.locator: Theorem 4.8, pp. 300–302; Corollaries 4.10–4.11, p. 302 (published version)
items.note: Rodríguez Camargo, Geometric Sen theory over rigid analytic spaces, Theorem 1.0.3 is the cited canonical-field supplier; Heuer Theorem 4.8 proves chart independence by twisting, with smallness arranged for each chart as in item 37. No local correspondence is applied to a bundle outside its small domain.

items.name: Definition 4.12 and Proposition 4.13: untwisting a pro-étale bundle
items.statement: For smooth rigid X/K, θ_V gives the coherent torsion-free algebra B_V=im(T_X→ν_*End(V)) with tautological section τ_{B_V}; put ℬ_V=ν^*B_V. If an invertible ℬ_V-module L satisfies HTlog(L)=τ_{B_V}, then V⊗_{ℬ_V}L^{-1} with the Higgs field θ_V⊗L^{-1} descends to an analytic Higgs bundle.
items.locator: Definition 4.12 and Proposition 4.13, p. 303 (published version)
items.note: Proposition 4.13 first yields étale-local analytic triviality after untwisting. The equivalence of analytic and étale vector bundles in item 60 completes the descent; it is already planned at H0 and R3.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (Theorem 1.1): the p-adic Simpson correspondence
items.statement: For smooth proper X over complete algebraically closed K/Q_p, a flat B_dR^+/ξ²-lift 𝕏 and an exponential Exp induce an exact tensor equivalence S_{𝕏,Exp}:Vect(X_proét,Ô_X)≃Higgs(X). It sends V to ν_*((V,θ_V)⊗_{ℬ_V}L_{B_V}^{−1}); its inverse sends (E,θ) to ν^*E⊗_{ℬ_θ}L_{B_θ}. For a continuous extension K→K′ of complete algebraically closed fields with Exp′|_K=Exp, smooth proper X′/K′ with lift 𝕏′, and f:X′→X admitting a lift f̃:𝕏′→𝕏, there is a natural transformation t_f̃:f^*∘S_{𝕏,Exp}⇒S_{𝕏′,Exp′}∘f^*, compatible with composition of lifted morphisms. The equivalence depends on 𝕏 and Exp (Remark 5.2). For connected X and x∈X(K), composing with the embedding of item 54 gives a fully faithful exact tensor functor Rep_K(π_1(X,x))→Higgs(X).
items.locator: Theorem 5.1, p. 304; proof pp. 304–306; Theorem 1.1 and §1.1, pp. 261–262 (published version)
items.note: The representation input has only the pro-finite-étale essential image; it is not an equivalence from representations to all pro-étale bundles. Theorem 5.1(2) makes naturality a transformation for the lifted data just specified, not a choice-free assertion for every f.

items.name: Proposition 5.3: deformation to the Higgs bundle
items.statement: In the smooth proper lifted setting of Theorem 5.1, for V and (E,θ)=S_{𝕏,Exp}(V), there are a connected smooth rigid space S/K, two K-points 0,s∈S(K), and a pro-étale vector bundle N on X×S with fibres N|_{X×{0}}≅ν^*E and N|_{X×{s}}≅V.
items.locator: Proposition 5.3, p. 306 (published version)

items.name: Dolbeault cohomology of a Higgs bundle
items.statement: For a Higgs bundle (E, θ) on a smooth rigid space X of dimension d, C*_Higgs(E, θ) = [E → E ⊗ Ω̃^1 → ··· → E ⊗ Ω̃^d] with θ_k(e ⊗ w) = θ(e) ∧ w, and RΓ_Higgs(X, (E, θ)) := RΓ(X_ét, C*_Higgs(E, θ)). As complexes on X_ét, C*_Higgs(E, θ) = RHom_{T_X}(O_X, E) for the T_X-module structure given by θ, computed by the Koszul resolution K• of O_X over T_X; hence RΓ_Higgs(X, (E, θ)) = RΓ(X_ét, RHom_{T_X}(O_X, E)).
items.locator: Definition 5.4, pp. 306–307 (published version)
items.note: The shared Koszul construction and change of generators are item 69, imported from DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1. The resolution uses the regular polynomial-coordinate sequence locally in T_X=Sym(Ω̃_X^∨); an arbitrary Koszul sequence need not resolve its quotient.

items.name: Theorem 5.5 (Theorem 1.4): the cohomological comparison
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 5.1, for V and (E,θ)=S_{𝕏,Exp}(V), there is a natural isomorphism Rν_*V≅C_Higgs^•(E,θ) in D(X_ét); consequently RΓ(X_proét,V)≅RΓ_Higgs(X,(E,θ)). For V=Ô_X this gives the lift-dependent split Hodge–Tate decomposition. The proof uses the adic completion of T_X along the spectral ideal, continuous cohomology on a toric tower, decompletion to the small representation E(U), and an exp/log change of Koszul generators on a disc of radius |p|^β with β>1/(p−1).
items.locator: Theorem 5.5 and Lemma 5.7, pp. 307–310; Theorem 1.4, p. 263 (published version)
items.note: Imports 46, 66–69, 75–76 distinguish Cartan–Leray, rational decompletion, bounded integral torsion, continuous Koszul computation, generic Koszul algebra, algebraic completion flatness and analytic flatness. Heuer cites Moduli spaces Lemma 6.7 in v1; it is Lemma 6.9 in v2, p. 38. The closed boundary radius in E4 is excluded; at p=2 the paper’s α=2 already suffices. CP.3 supplies the spectral sequence only, not this splitting.

items.name: Pro-étale base change for a coherent algebra over a proper space
items.statement: Let X/K be proper rigid, B coherent on X, Y/K smooth, and π_Y:X×Y→Y. For the completed pro-étale pullback ℬ of B, π_{Y,proét*}ℬ≅H^0(X,B)⊗_KÔ_{Y}, compatibly with base change.
items.locator: Heuer §2.3, equation (6), pp. 274–275; Heuer, The relative Hodge–Tate spectral sequence for rigid analytic spaces, Theorem 3.18(c).
items.note: This relative completed-sheaf application remains at the later P8 suffix. It is distinct from item 10’s coherent analytic base change and item 6’s local comparison used upstream of CP.3.

items.name: The étale site of a rigid space and of its diamond
items.statement: For a rigid K-space X, diamondification induces equivalences X_ét≃X^◇_ét and X_fét≃X^◇_fét (Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds, Lemma 15.6).
items.locator: Heuer proofs of Theorem 2.4(3–5), p. 281, and Theorem 3.2, pp. 284–285; Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds, Lemma 15.6.
items.note: D6 plans the étale and finite étale site equivalences. Full faithfulness of seminormal rigid spaces over Spd K is a different missing theorem, item 53.

items.name: Cartan–Leray on the perfectoid toric tower
items.statement: Let f:U→T^d be a toric chart on smooth affinoid U/K and Ũ→U its affinoid perfectoid Δ=Z_p(1)^d-torsor. For a pro-étale vector bundle V trivialized on Ũ, acyclicity of finite free Ô-modules on the affinoid perfectoid tower identifies RΓ(U_proét,V) with RΓ_cts(Δ,V(Ũ)).
items.locator: Heuer proof of Lemma 5.7, p. 310; Heuer, Moduli spaces, arXiv:2207.13819v1 Lemma 6.7 = v2 Lemma 6.9, p. 38.
items.note: Cartan–Leray alone has tower coefficients. The proof needs the additional rational decompletion RΓ_cts(Δ,E(U))≅RΓ_cts(Δ,V(Ũ)), item 66, with bounded-torsion integral input 67 and topology-sensitive Koszul computation 68. AI.3 supplies the perfectoid acyclicity, not a duplicate construction here.

items.name: Almost purity
items.statement: For a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra R and finite étale R-algebra S, S is perfectoid and S^{∘a} is finite étale over R^{∘a} (Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Theorem 7.9(iii)). In the affinoid perfectoid pro-finite-étale tower used in Proposition 2.9(i), reduction modulo p^k of the completed integral sheaves is computed by the filtered finite-level maps, which are almost finite étale.
items.locator: Heuer proof of Proposition 2.9(i), p. 273; Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Theorem 7.9; the source’s Theorem 5.2 citation is E6.
items.note: Added in review. PerfectoidSpaces P3 plans ECD Theorem 6.1 (almost purity and étale tilting).

items.name: Pro-étale cohomology of pulled-back étale sheaves
items.statement: For an abelian sheaf F on X_ét and a quasi-compact quasi-separated U=lim_j U_j in X_proét, H^i(U,ν^{-1}F)=colim_j H^i(U_j,F). Consequently F→Rν_*ν^{-1}F is an isomorphism (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Lemma 3.16 and Corollary 3.17).
items.locator: Heuer proof of Lemma 2.8, pp. 270–272; Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Lemma 3.16 and Corollary 3.17.
items.note: Reuse ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0 continuity under cofiltered limits, following PAPER-SCHOLZE-13’s planned status for these precise inputs.

items.name: Affinoid perfectoid basis of the rigid pro-étale site
items.statement: For smooth rigid X/K, affinoid perfectoid objects form a basis of X_proét. Locally one obtains them from the completed p-power toric tower over a toric chart; the associated perfectoid affinoid is independent of the presentation.
items.locator: Heuer proof of Proposition 2.9(i), p. 273; Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Corollary 4.7 and Proposition 4.8.
items.note: Requested extension of AInfCohomology AI.3 from smooth formal generic fibres to this rigid-space scope; coordinate PAPER-SCHOLZE-13 route 5 and the AI.3 request in PadicHodgeTheory--P7. The existing request does not make the broader result planned.

items.name: Perfectoid vector-bundle descent across analytic, étale, pro-étale and v-sites
items.statement: For a perfectoid space Y, finite locally free O-modules on its analytic, étale, pro-étale and v-sites have equivalent categories. If Y is affinoid perfectoid these categories are equivalent to finite projective O(Y)-modules.
items.locator: Kedlaya–Liu, Relative p-adic Hodge theory II: imperfect period rings, arXiv:1602.06899, Theorem 3.5.8, PDF p. 76; cited in Heuer §2.1, pp. 267–268.
items.note: One requested early generic supplier at DiamondsAndVStacks D2. Coordinate PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20/121 and its RF2/VB1 applications: those later applications import this theorem, and cannot be imported back into D2. PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/373 remains a separate gluing request, not evidence of a planned full site equivalence.

items.name: Transfer of perfectoid vector-bundle descent to rigid X
items.statement: For rigid X/K, restriction and descent through its affinoid perfectoid pro-étale basis identify finite locally free Ô_X-modules on the flattened X_proét with v-vector bundles on Perf_K/X. This also identifies the vector-bundle categories obtained from the pro-étale-site variants used in §2.1.
items.locator: Heuer §2.1, pp. 267–268; Heuer, Moduli spaces in p-adic non-abelian Hodge theory, arXiv:2207.13819v2, §1.1.
items.note: Downstream Simpson input: imports items 1, 49 and 50. D2 supplies only the generic perfectoid theorem, not the rigid flattened site or its completed sheaf.

items.name: First-order de Rham period sheaf with its square-zero kernel
items.statement: On X_proét for smooth rigid X/K there is a surjection θ:B_dR^+/ξ²→Ô_X whose kernel (ξ)/(ξ²) is canonically Ô_X(1). The map from the Tate twist sends a compatible p-power root-of-unity system ε to [ε]−1 modulo ξ²; this is the inverse direction to gr^1 B_dR≅Ô_X(1).
items.locator: Heuer Definition 2.12 and Lemmas 2.13/2.16, pp. 275–278; PadicHodgeTheory--P7, period-sheaves-on-affinoid-perfectoids and graded-de-rham-period-sheaf-tate-twist.
items.note: Import the sheaf-level θ and twist interface. A ring named BDeRhamPlus at the pin does not supply this pro-étale sheaf theorem.

items.name: Full faithfulness of rigid diamondification over Spd K
items.statement: The diamondification functor from seminormal rigid spaces over K to diamonds OVER Spd K is fully faithful. In particular maps between smooth rigid K-spaces can be recovered with their K-structure from those diamonds.
items.locator: Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley Lectures on p-adic Geometry, Proposition 10.2.3, printed p. 78; used in Heuer §2.1 and representability arguments, pp. 267, 281, 284–285.
items.note: Requested DiamondsAndVStacks D6 extension, separate from item 45’s site equivalence. Coordinate PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26/026 and PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20/69 so the generic theorem has one owner; the latter’s Part II proposal is not an already planned D6 node.

items.name: Representations and pro-finite-étale vector bundles
items.statement: For connected smooth proper X/K with x∈X(K), descent from the universal pro-finite-étale cover gives an exact tensor equivalence between finite-dimensional continuous K-representations of π_1(X,x) and v-vector bundles trivialized by that cover. Via item 51 this embeds as a full exact tensor subcategory of pro-étale vector bundles.
items.locator: Heuer, Line bundles on rigid spaces in the v-topology, arXiv:2012.07918v2, Theorem 5.2, p. 22; Heuer Simpson paper, pp. 261–262.
items.note: The essential image is pro-finite-étale, not all v- or pro-étale vector bundles. Item 40 composes this embedding with Simpson.

items.name: Picard representability for an arbitrary proper scheme over a field
items.statement: For a proper K-scheme Z, the relative Picard functor Pic_{Z/K} is represented by a group scheme locally of finite type over K. Z and its Picard scheme need not be smooth or connected.
items.locator: Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models, §8.2, Theorem 3, p. 211 (cleared copy); Heuer §2.2, p. 268, with citation corrected by E1.
items.note: Requested general Picard supplier in AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2 covers an abelian degree-zero case and cannot supply this theorem. Only the algebraisable example in Theorem 2.4 needs it; the main representable reduction does not.

items.name: Relative coherent GAGA and algebraization of finite coherent algebras
items.statement: For a proper scheme over an affinoid K-algebra, analytification is an exact tensor equivalence on coherent modules, with comparison of coherent higher direct images. Consequently finite coherent algebras, their finite relative spectra and the line bundles used to identify the relative Picard functors algebraize.
items.locator: Heuer §2.2 and proof of Theorem 2.4, pp. 268, 281; AdicSpacesPartII--R3, proper-gaga and proper-gaga-coherent-equivalence.
items.note: Reuse R3’s relative coherent theorem; no new GAGA construction in the Simpson Part II.

items.name: Gerritzen’s disc Picard decomposition
items.statement: For rigid analytic Z and the closed unit disc E, line bundles on Z×E are locally trivial over Z. If G_1 is the sheaf of disc units with constant coefficient 1 and all other coefficients pointwise of norm <1, then Pic(Z×E)≅Pic(Z)⊕H^1(Z,G_1). In Heuer’s use, a homomorphism G_a^+→Pic_{X′} thereby yields a class in H^1(X′,1+m_K O^+), to which log applies.
items.locator: Gerritzen, Zerlegungen der Picard-Gruppe nichtarchimedischer holomorpher Räume, Compositio Math. 35 (1977), §2 Satz 1, p. 28, and §3 Satz 2, p. 31; Heuer Lemma 2.23, p. 282.
items.note: Read the public Numdam article, including the p. 31 image. The Picard-Lie identification in item 25 uses this result together with item 77; neither is supplied merely by naming Fargues.

items.name: Openness of étale maps of analytic adic spaces
items.statement: An étale morphism of analytic adic spaces is open on underlying topological spaces. Thus a map induced by [p] on a representable rigid Picard group has open image once its derivative is invertible.
items.locator: Heuer proof of Theorem 2.4, p. 281; Huber, Étale Cohomology of Rigid Analytic Varieties and Adic Spaces, Proposition 1.7.8; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.
items.note: Openness alone does not imply that an arbitrary analytic subgroup is closed. The Picard [p]-image is closed by its locally constant Kummer boundary, as in item 24.

items.name: Kummer and analytic Picard comparison in characteristic zero
items.statement: For a rigid K-space Z and n≥1, the étale sequence 1→μ_n→O_Z^×→^{n}O_Z^×→1 is exact, and H^1_ét(Z,O_Z^×)=Pic_an(Z). This includes n=p^a since p is invertible in O_Z, although p is not invertible in O_Z^+.
items.locator: Heuer proof of Corollary 2.19, pp. 279–280; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0, kummer-sequence.

items.name: Analytic–étale vector-bundle comparison and split additive/multiplicative torsors
items.statement: On locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces, analytic vector bundles and étale vector bundles are equivalent, and for an analytic vector bundle E the derived pushforward of its étale pullback is E. Hence H^1_an(Z,O_Z)=H^1_ét(Z,O_Z) and H^1_an(Z,O_Z^×)=H^1_ét(Z,O_Z^×); étale torsors under G_a^r×G_m^s are analytically locally trivial.
items.locator: Heuer Theorem 3.14 and Proposition 4.13/Theorem 5.1, pp. 289–291, 303–305; Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Lemma 7.3; H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles and kummer-sequence; R3/finite-projective-etale-descent.
items.note: These contracts work over the complete K in this paper; no arithmetic-model widening is needed. Arbitrary coherent B is a distinct extension, item 65.

items.name: Picard representability transfer through diamonds
items.statement: For connected smooth proper X over a perfectoid K, the étale diamantine Picard functor is the diamondification of the rigid Picard functor; representability by a rigid group transfers in either direction, and representability of the étale and v-Picard functors is equivalent. Heuer transports the argument to the coherent-algebra Picard extension in Theorem 2.4 rather than assuming smoothness of its finite spectral space X′.
items.locator: Heuer, Diamantine Picard functors of rigid spaces, arXiv:2103.16557v4, Corollary 2.9(3–5), §2, PDF p. 7 (proof p. 28); Heuer Simpson paper, proof of Theorem 2.4 after diagram (8), p. 281.
items.note: The cited corollary itself has smooth proper hypotheses. Do not attribute the full possibly singular X′ generalization to that corollary without the separate argument in Heuer Theorem 2.4.

items.name: Formal models for coherent modules on a quasi-compact smooth rigid space
items.statement: For smooth quasi-compact rigid X/K and coherent B, choose an admissible formal model 𝔛 of X with a finitely presented O_𝔛-module 𝔅 whose generic fibre is B. On X_an, O_X^+⊗_{η^{-1}O_𝔛}η^{-1}𝔅 is a finitely presented integral model; quotienting its p-power torsion gives its image in B.
items.locator: Heuer Lemma 2.7 and proof, pp. 269–270, public restatement of Abbes, Éléments de géométrie rigide I, Proposition 4.8.18(ii).
items.note: Requested R2/R3 formal-model input. The Abbes book is not cleared and was not read; this records only the public restatement and its use, leaving that proof supplier explicit.

items.name: Finite formal models for a finite spectral morphism
items.statement: For X as in item 62 and a coherent O_X-algebra B, the finite morphism X′=Spa_{O_X}(B)→X has, after choosing compatible admissible formal models, a finite formal morphism f:𝔛′→𝔛 with generic fibre X′→X. The finite O_𝔛-algebra f_*O_𝔛′ gives the algebra version of the integral model in Lemma 2.7.
items.locator: Heuer proof of Lemma 2.7, pp. 269–270, invoking Abbes, Éléments de géométrie rigide I, Proposition 5.9.17 and Theorem 2.11.5.
items.note: Requested R2/R3 extension, separate from the module case. Only Heuer’s public restatement was read; the uncleared book remains an unread proof supplier.

items.name: Generic freeness in the Noetherian-domain finite-module case
items.statement: If R is a Noetherian domain and M is a finite R-module, some nonzero r∈R has M_r free over R_r. Apply Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers with S=nonZeroDivisors R, R_s=FractionRing R and the localized module: finite implies finitely presented, and the module over the fraction field is free.
items.locator: Heuer Lemma 3.5, p. 287, citing Stacks Project Tag 051S; Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/Free.lean at 082e2d3.
items.note: Read all localization/scalar-tower/Nontrivial hypotheses. This is the special case used here, not a claim that Mathlib formalizes arbitrary R→S generic freeness; no instantiation was compiled. Item 28 supplies the connected domain component.

items.name: Analytic–étale comparison for arbitrary coherent modules
items.statement: For a coherent module B on a rigid K-space X, analytic and étale coherent descent and local finite presentations give Rλ_*λ^*B≅B; in particular H^1_an(X,B)≅H^1_ét(X,B). This applies to a coherent finite spectral algebra B even when it is not locally free.
items.locator: Heuer Lemma 2.23 and Theorem 2.4(4), pp. 281–282; used coherent refinement of the analytic–étale comparison.
items.note: Requested R3 extension using H0 locally acyclic finite free presentations. The existing H0 finite-projective theorem (item 60) alone is not this coherent contract. Keep this extra supplier visible for the Lie comparison.

items.name: Rational toric decompletion for a small representation
items.statement: Let U=Spa(R,R^+) have a toric Δ=Z_p(1)^d-tower with completed ring R_∞. With the small integral representation and lattices of item 67, extension of coefficients induces RΓ_cts(Δ,E(U))≅RΓ_cts(Δ,R_∞⊗_R E(U)) after inverting p, for E(U)=R^n with that action.
items.locator: Heuer proof of Lemma 5.7, p. 310; Heuer, Moduli spaces, arXiv:2207.13819v1 Lemma 6.7 = v2 Lemma 6.9, p. 38.
items.note: This removes tower coefficients, a step Cartan–Leray alone does not give. Coordinate the shared geometric-tower supplier PhiGammaModulesPartIIGeometricTowers (PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17 route 15) and AI.3 estimates; the Simpson application adds its particular small representation.

items.name: Uniform integral torsion bound underlying decompletion
items.statement: With R,R_∞,Δ as above and a continuous representation ρ:Δ→GL_n(R^+) satisfying ρ≡1 mod p^α for the technical smallness constant in Moduli spaces §3, set M=(R^+)^n or (R^+/p^k)^n with this action and the diagonal action on R_∞^+⊗M. For every m the comparison of continuous cohomology from M to tower coefficients has kernel and cokernel killed by p^c, with c independent of k. In degree zero the comparison is an integral isomorphism.
items.locator: Heuer, Moduli spaces, arXiv:2207.13819v2, Lemma 6.9, p. 38 (v1 Lemma 6.7, p. 37); used in Heuer Simpson Lemma 5.7.
items.note: The nonintegral-monomial summand has uniformly bounded p-power-torsion cohomology, using the AI.3 toric estimates. Do not replace this with integral isomorphisms in every degree. Coordinate the geometric-tower decompletion owner; α here is the cited technical bound, not automatically 1/(p−1).

items.name: Continuous Z_p^d cohomology as a Koszul complex
items.statement: Let Δ=Z_p^d and N=lim_k N_k with its inverse-limit topology, where N_k are discrete continuous Δ-modules killed by p^k. The continuous cochains for Δ are quasi-isomorphic to the Koszul cochain complex for the commuting γ_i−1. In the toric application use the complete lattice with its p-power quotients first; rationalization uses the additional bounded-torsion estimates of items 66–67.
items.locator: Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, proof of Lemma 5.5; Heuer, Moduli spaces, arXiv:2207.13819v2, Lemmas 6.9/6.11, p. 38; Heuer Simpson Lemma 5.7, p. 310.
items.note: Exact existing supplier: AInfCohomology:AI.1/continuous-cochains-koszul in AInfCohomology--AI.0. It reuses the Mathlib continuousCohomology carrier and DD.1 Koszul complex. Its inverse-limit topology is essential; it does not assert a comparison for arbitrary abstract modules. Coordinate the broader ArithmeticGaloisDuality topological-coefficient supplier, without duplicating this planned lattice theorem.

items.name: Shared Koszul complex and invertible change of generators
items.statement: For a finite family of commuting endomorphisms of a module, form the Koszul cochain complex with exterior-power terms. Multiplying each operator by a commuting unit gives a chain isomorphism, with the induced product of those units in each exterior degree. For the regular polynomial-coordinate sequence the Koszul complex also resolves its quotient; arbitrary sequences need not do so.
items.locator: Heuer Definition 5.4 and proof of Lemma 5.7, pp. 307–310; Stacks Project Tags 0621/0625; DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1 and PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17/P16.
items.note: Reuse the shared DD.1 algebra and its accepted commuting-endomorphism request. The exp/log quotient is a unit only on the strict smaller radius in E4.

items.name: Toric charts for smooth affinoid rigid spaces
items.statement: Let U/K be smooth affinoid of pure dimension d over a complete nonarchimedean field. Every point has a rational neighbourhood admitting an étale map to T^d which is a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps. Such charts cover smooth rigid spaces and can be chosen inside a prescribed open neighbourhood.
items.locator: Heuer Definition 4.3, p. 298; PadicHodgeTheory--P7, toric-charts-for-smooth-spaces.
items.note: Only the geometry is imported here; the chart-dependent Higgs lattice, ρ_f and quantitative smallness are item 35. The perfectoid tower reuses item 49.

items.name: Proper singular mod-p finiteness and primitive almost comparison
items.statement: For proper rigid Z over complete algebraically closed K/Q_p, with no smoothness assumption, H^i_ét(Z,F_p) is finite-dimensional and the map H^i_ét(Z,F_p)⊗_{F_p}O_K/p→H^i_ét(Z,O_Z^+/p) is an almost isomorphism. Étale cohomology is invariant under reduction, so the finiteness statement applies to the possibly non-reduced finite spectral space X′.
items.locator: Scholze, Perfectoid spaces: a survey, Theorem 3.17 and proof, PDF pp. 19–20; used in Heuer Corollary 2.19, p. 279.
items.note: Requested early P8:local-rational extension, coordinated with item 6 and BMS18 route 14. The singular proof uses rigid resolution with SNC boundary (item 72), not just the smooth theorem or algebraic R09.7. Nilpotent invariance is item 73.

items.name: SNC-boundary refinement for rigid resolution in singular comparison
items.statement: The characteristic-zero rigid resolution input used in the proper singular primitive-comparison proof replaces a reduced rigid space by a proper smooth modification over its regular locus, and resolves the exceptional/boundary locus so the boundary on the smooth space is a strict normal-crossings divisor. Induction and proper descent then reduce the comparison to smooth and boundary strata.
items.locator: Scholze, Perfectoid spaces: a survey, proof of Theorem 3.17, PDF pp. 19–20 and footnote 3 (Bierstone–Milman); related unread rigid-resolution gap in AdicSpacesPartII.
items.note: Item 88 now supplies the accepted rigid smooth-modification theorem at AdicSpacesPartIIPartII RZ.5. Request its SNC-boundary refinement for this comparison proof there, rather than treating algebraic R09.7 as an analytic theorem or replanning the existing resolution. Neither the RZ.5 node nor the PD.7 proof-closure gap G3 is a closed proof of the full SNC dévissage. The original cited rigid-resolution proof was not newly read.

items.name: Nilpotent invariance of the rigid étale site
items.statement: A nilpotent closed immersion Z_red→Z of rigid spaces induces an equivalence of étale sites, hence preserves torsion étale cohomology. In particular the finite spectral space used for Kummer finiteness can first be reduced.
items.locator: Scholze, Perfectoid spaces: a survey, proof of Theorem 3.17, pp. 19–20; Heuer Remark 2.6 and Corollary 2.19, pp. 270, 279.
items.note: Explicit requested H0 extension in this extraction; no additional planned contract is inferred from a general mention of étale geometry.

items.name: Square-zero smooth lifting and existence of lifted rigidifying points
items.statement: A flat locally finitely presented thickening 𝕏 over B_dR^+/ξ² whose K-fibre X is smooth is smooth over that square-zero base. Formal smoothness therefore lifts each x∈X(K) to a point of 𝕏(B_dR^+/ξ²). The analogous infinitesimal lifting property gives the local period-algebra maps in Lemma 2.13. A finite set of points can be lifted individually; there is no asserted canonical choice.
items.locator: Heuer Lemma 2.13 and proof of Theorem 3.22, pp. 276, 295–296.
items.note: A separate used input from existence of 𝕏. The finite-presentation/smooth-thickening assumptions are retained; point lifts are the extra data 𝕄 in items 28/32.

items.name: Noetherian finite-polynomial adic completion is flat
items.statement: If R is Noetherian and I an ideal, Module.Flat R (AdicCompletion I R). If A is Noetherian and the variable type is finite, MvPolynomial σ A is Noetherian. Thus on an affinoid trivialization, affinoid Noetherianity and these declarations supply flatness of the J-adic completion of the finite-polynomial local spectral algebra T_X.
items.locator: Heuer Theorem 5.5, pp. 307–308; Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/AsTensorProduct.lean and Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Basic.lean at 082e2d3.
items.note: Read the Noetherian and finite-variable hypotheses. The statement is an algebraic input, not analytic Tate-algebra flatness or sheaf transport. No Lean instantiation was compiled.

items.name: Analytic Tate-algebra flatness and transport to the completed spectral sheaf
items.statement: The analytic map from the local polynomial spectral algebra to the sufficiently small-radius Tate algebra used in Lemma 5.7 is flat. The local J-adic-completion maps and these analytic flat maps glue and remain suitable for the tensor/base-change steps defining the completed spectral sheaf and comparing its Koszul complexes.
items.locator: Heuer proof of Theorem 5.5 and Lemma 5.7, pp. 307–310.
items.note: Separate missing analytic/sheaf interfaces; item 75’s algebraic instances alone do not establish them. Use a radius strictly smaller than the exponential threshold, as in E4.

items.name: Lie algebra via homomorphisms from a small additive disc
items.statement: A commutative rigid group over K has an affinoid open subgroup isomorphic to an additive polydisc. Consequently, with G_a^+ the additive unit disc, Lie(G)≅Hom(G_a^+,G)[1/p]; maps become linear on a sufficiently small disc and restriction gives the p-localization.
items.locator: Fargues, Groupes analytiques rigides p-divisibles, author PDF, Corollaire 4, p. 16; Heuer Lemma 2.23, equation (9), p. 282.
items.note: The local-polydisc theorem is Fargues’s statement; the Hom description is the consequence explicitly used by Heuer. Do not subsume the separate Gerritzen input in this citation.

items.name: Lie criterion for an étale morphism of rigid groups
items.statement: A morphism between rigid analytic groups over a characteristic-zero nonarchimedean field is étale exactly when its derivative on Lie algebras is an isomorphism. For a commutative rigid group the derivative of [p] is multiplication by p, so [p] is étale.
items.locator: Fargues, Groupes analytiques rigides p-divisibles, author PDF, Lemme 1, p. 10; used in Heuer Corollary 2.19 and §3.3, pp. 279, 293.

items.name: Representable open topological p-torsion subgroup
items.statement: For a commutative rigid group G/K, the v-sheaf image of evaluation at 1 from Hom(Z_p,G)→G is represented by an open rigid subgroup Ĝ⊆G. Equivalently, its sections become arbitrarily small after iterated multiplication by p, locally on the test object.
items.locator: Heuer, A geometric p-adic Simpson correspondence in rank one, Proposition 2.14; Heuer–Werner–Zhang, arXiv:2308.13456v2, Definition 6.4 and Proposition 6.5(1), pp. 31–32; Heuer Simpson §3.3, p. 293.

items.name: Logarithm on the topological p-torsion subgroup
items.statement: For commutative rigid G/K, there is a unique morphism log_G:Ĝ→Lie(G)⊗G_a whose derivative is the identity, with kernel G[p^∞]. Thus 0→G[p^∞]→Ĝ→Lie(G)⊗G_a is left exact. Surjectivity is an additional local-p-divisibility condition, not automatic.
items.locator: Heuer–Werner–Zhang, arXiv:2308.13456v2, Proposition 6.5(2), pp. 31–32, and Proposition 6.10; Fargues, author PDF, Théorème 1.2, p. 17; Heuer Simpson §3.3, p. 293.

items.name: Finite-kernel criterion for a surjective étale group map
items.statement: For a surjective étale morphism of rigid analytic groups, the morphism is finite if and only if its kernel is finite. Apply this only after sheaf-surjectivity has been established, in particular in the corrected Pic^0 argument.
items.locator: Fargues, Groupes analytiques rigides p-divisibles, author PDF, Lemme 5, p. 11; Heuer Corollary 2.19, p. 279.

items.name: Existence of an exponential for algebraically closed K
items.statement: If K is complete algebraically closed over Q_p, there exists a group-homomorphic splitting Exp:K→1+m_K of log which agrees with the convergent series on the small subgroup in Definition 3.19. The choice is not canonical.
items.locator: Heuer–Werner–Zhang, arXiv:2308.13456v2, Lemma 6.2, p. 30; Heuer Definition 3.19, p. 293.

items.name: Proper pushforward preserves locally bounded Zariski constructibility
items.statement: For a proper map f:X→Y of rigid spaces over a characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean field with residue characteristic p, and any n≥1, Rf_* sends D^(b)_zc(X,Z/n) to D^(b)_zc(Y,Z/n). The notation means locally bounded constructible complexes, not a global uniform boundedness claim on non-quasi-compact spaces.
items.locator: Bhatt–Hansen, The six functors for Zariski-constructible sheaves in rigid geometry, arXiv:2101.09759, Theorem 3.10, PDF pp. 17–18; used in the proof of Theorem 3.15, p. 20.
items.note: Supplier of overconvergence in the p-primary proper-base-change proof; route 6 owns this explicit extension beyond its smooth-proper endpoint. The accepted ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomologyPartII packet now states this exact target at PD.7/proper-constructible-pushforward; reuse it, retaining its explicit G3 singular-comparison proof-supplier gap.

items.name: Cartesian proper base change including p-primary coefficients
items.statement: For a Cartesian square of rigid K-spaces with f:X→Y proper and base change g:Y′→Y, the map g^*Rf_*F→Rf′_*g′^*F is an isomorphism for every F∈D^(b)_zc(X,Z/n), n≥1. No smoothness or reducedness hypothesis is imposed on X.
items.locator: Bhatt–Hansen, The six functors for Zariski-constructible sheaves in rigid geometry, Theorem 3.15, PDF p. 20; Heuer Proposition 2.18, p. 279.
items.note: For n prime to p use H3’s proper-support base change. For n=p^a the proof needs item 85, Huber’s rank-one geometric-stalk formula (Example 2.6.2, p. 139, read in cleared copy) and item 87. Item 12 is only its constant-family specialization. The accepted ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomologyPartII packet now states this exact target at PD.7/proper-base-change-all-torsion; reuse it, retaining its explicit G3 singular-comparison proof-supplier gap.

items.name: Proper p-primary cohomology invariant under algebraically closed field extension
items.statement: For a continuous extension C→C′ of complete algebraically closed extensions of Q_p, proper rigid Z/C, a≥1 and F∈D^b_zc(Z,Z/p^a), the map RΓ_ét(Z,F)→RΓ_ét(Z_C′,F_C′) is an isomorphism, including singular Z.
items.locator: Bhatt–Hansen, The six functors for Zariski-constructible sheaves in rigid geometry, Lemma 3.25 and proof, PDF p. 25.
items.note: Uses proper primitive comparison, including the singular supplier in item 71. D^b here is the bounded proper-space case; do not substitute it for the locally bounded D^(b) in Theorems 3.10/3.15. The accepted ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomologyPartII packet now states this exact target at PD.7/proper-field-extension; reuse it, retaining its explicit G3 singular-comparison proof-supplier gap.

items.name: Proper rigid resolution in characteristic zero
items.statement: For a quasi-compact reduced rigid space Z over a characteristic-zero complete nonarchimedean field, a finite sequence of rigid blow-ups with smooth centres gives a proper smooth modification Z̃→Z which is an isomorphism over the regular locus. The general locally finite hypersequence construction is compatible with smooth maps and complete field extensions.
items.locator: AdicSpacesPartIIPartII:RZ.5/rigid-resolution and resolution-consequences; Temkin, Functorial desingularization of quasi-excellent schemes in characteristic zero: the nonembedded case, Theorems 5.2.2/5.3.2 as identified in the accepted packet.
items.note: Read the accepted packet’s exact rigid theorem, not merely algebraic R09.7. This supplies the smooth modification in item 72; an SNC boundary compatible with the comparison dévissage is a separately requested extension. The Temkin proof was not newly read in this fix.

routes.title: P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison, Part II: the p-adic Simpson correspondence for smooth proper rigid spaces
routes.brief: Continue P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory) with Heuer’s non-abelian comparison for smooth proper rigid X over complete algebraically closed K/Q_p. For a flat B_dR^+/ξ²-lift 𝕏 and a group-homomorphic splitting Exp of log that agrees with the convergent exponential on p^α m_K (α=1/(p−1) for p≥3, α=2 for p=2), Theorem 5.1 gives an exact tensor equivalence S_{𝕏,Exp}:Vect(X_proét,Ô_X)≃Higgs(X). For a continuous extension K→K′ of complete algebraically closed fields with Exp′|_K=Exp, smooth proper X′/K′ with lift 𝕏′, and f:X′→X admitting a lift f̃:𝕏′→𝕏, there is a natural transformation t_f̃:f^*∘S_{𝕏,Exp}⇒S_{𝕏′,Exp′}∘f^*, compatible with composition of lifted morphisms. The equivalence depends on 𝕏 and Exp (Remark 5.2). Theorem 5.5 identifies Rν_*V with the Higgs complex of S(V) in D(X_ét), hence identifies derived global cohomology. Its V=Ô_X case is the lift-dependent split Hodge–Tate decomposition; the CP.3 spectral sequence alone does not give that splitting. Proposition 5.3 gives a connected smooth parameter space S with K-points 0,s and a bundle N on X×S specializing to ν^*E and V. Build six layers: (1) rigid pro-étale vector bundles and their perfectoid/v transfer, importing the common Higgs definition, then spectral algebras B_θ and τ; (2) coherent-algebra Picard functors, integral models on the distinct sites, logarithm-normalized Hodge–Tate sequences and the Higgs–Tate torsor; (3) the always-representable P_𝕏 and finite rigidifying multisets with chosen point lifts 𝕄, including the derivative comparison for forgetful maps; (4) topological p-torsion, the logarithm sequence and the proven locally p-divisible exponential theorem, producing functorial L_B for coherent torsion-free T_X-algebras, with maximal torsion-free pullback/product quotients and the sum tautological section; (5) chart-dependent ρ_f, lattices, quantitative smallness, the inverse local correspondence, canonical Higgs fields and untwisting; (6) the global equivalence, deformation and derived cohomology. Use the corrected Pic^0[p]-torsor group and the sheaf-theoretic surjectivity repair; finite components are required for stronger whole-group p-divisibility assertions. Openness alone is not a closed-subgroup argument. The finite-étaleness conclusion used downstream survives.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 3.20, arXiv v3 p. 22; published p. 293
sourceIssues.printed: The attributed rigid-group exponential theorem assumes only that [p] is surjective on K-points.
sourceIssues.correction: Extract the cited HWZ Theorem 6.12 with G locally p-divisible (equivalently its logarithm surjective as an étale sheaf); a justification for the broader printed attribution is missing.
sourceIssues.reason: The cited proof uses the analytic p-divisible identity component. K-point surjectivity does not supply that hypothesis: the open subgroup of G_a given by radius-one discs centred at all K-points has all K-points but misses extension-valued points far from K, so its logarithm inclusion is not sheaf-surjective. Its K-point splitting is nevertheless the identity, so this is not a counterexample to the K-point conclusion. The actual P_𝕏^0 and (P_𝕏^M)^0 applications have the stronger proven hypothesis.
